items.stem: A user says 'I would definitely pay for this' when shown a mock-up. Why should a researcher treat this with caution?

options.text: Stated future purchase intent is a weak predictor of actual behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: people routinely overstate willingness to pay for hypothetical products.

options.text: Mock-ups are never allowed in interviews
options.rationale: Mock-ups are a valid stimulus; the issue is the type of claim, not the artefact.
The user may be sincere; intent simply does not reliably predict action.

options.text: Payment questions are illegal in research
options.rationale: There is no such prohibition; the concern is predictive validity.

items.explanation: Correct: people routinely overstate willingness to pay for hypothetical products.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which practices strengthen the validity of a customer discovery study? (Select TWO)

options.text: Recruiting participants who match the real target segment
options.rationale: Correct: a representative sample makes findings generalisable to the intended users.

options.text: Asking about specific past behaviour rather than hypothetical futures
options.rationale: Correct: recalled behaviour is a better evidence base than speculation.

options.text: Interviewing only enthusiastic supporters of the idea
options.rationale: This introduces confirmation bias and inflates apparent demand.

options.text: Stopping after the first interview that confirms the hypothesis
options.rationale: One confirming case is anecdote, not validation.

items.explanation: Correct: a representative sample makes findings generalisable to the intended users.

items.stem: During synthesis a team keeps only the three quotes that support launching the product and discards contradicting notes. What error is this?

options.rationale: Correct: selectively retaining supportive evidence distorts the conclusion.
Discarding disconfirming data is not prioritisation; it hides risk.
Saturation is reaching no new themes, not ignoring inconvenient ones.
Triangulation combines sources; here evidence is being suppressed.
